rubric.why: Identifies the organisms grouped in a species and their ability to reproduce.
rubric.description: A species is a group of similar organisms capable of interbreeding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a group of similar organisms that can interbreed.

rubric.why: Fertility of the offspring is a key part of the biological species definition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that interbreeding produces fertile offspring.

modelAnswer: A species is a group of similar organisms that can interbreed.

items.followUp: State one difference between a plant cell wall and a cell membrane.

rubric.why: The primary wall is deposited while the cell is growing and remains relatively thin and flexible.
rubric.description: The primary cell wall is thin and is formed during cell growth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the primary wall as thin, flexible, or formed during growth.

rubric.why: The secondary wall is deposited after growth and adds thickness and strength.
rubric.description: The secondary cell wall is deposited inside the primary wall after growth and is thicker.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating its position, timing, or greater thickness.

modelAnswer: The primary cell wall is thin and flexible and forms while the cell is growing.
The secondary cell wall is deposited inside the primary wall after growth and is thicker and more rigid.

items.followUp: What is the role of turgor pressure in a plant cell?

rubric.why: Turgor pressure is defined by the force exerted by the cell contents on the cell wall.
rubric.description: Turgor pressure is the pressure exerted by the cell contents against the cell wall.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying pressure exerted by the cell contents or cytoplasm against the cell wall.

rubric.why: Water entering the cell creates the pressure against the wall.
rubric.description: It develops when water enters the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking turgor pressure to water entering or being taken up by the cell.

modelAnswer: Turgor pressure is the pressure exerted by the cell contents against the cell wall.
It develops when water enters the cell.

items.followUp: Differentiate between asexual and sexual reproduction.

rubric.why: Germline cells give rise to reproductive cells or gametes.
rubric.description: Germline cells form gametes and pass genetic information to offspring.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that germline cells form gametes or transmit genetic information to offspring.

rubric.why: Somatic cells make up the body and are distinct from reproductive germline cells.
rubric.description: Somatic cells are body cells other than germline cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying somatic cells as body cells that are not germline cells.

modelAnswer: Germline cells form gametes and pass genetic information to offspring.
Somatic cells are body cells other than germline cells.

items.followUp: Name one organism that can reproduce by regeneration.

rubric.why: Regeneration involves regrowing or replacing a lost body part.
rubric.description: Regeneration is the regrowth or replacement of a lost body part.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning regrowth or replacement of a body part.

rubric.why: In some organisms, regeneration from a body fragment can produce a complete organism.
rubric.description: In some organisms, a body fragment can develop into a complete organism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that a fragment may grow into a complete organism.

modelAnswer: Regeneration is the regrowth or replacement of a lost body part.
In some organisms, a body fragment can develop into a complete organism.

items.followUp: What are the products of lactic acid fermentation?

rubric.why: Alcoholic fermentation is an anaerobic process involving the breakdown of glucose.
rubric.description: Alcoholic fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glucose is broken down without oxygen.

rubric.why: Ethanol and carbon dioxide are the characteristic products of alcoholic fermentation.
rubric.description: It produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both products.

modelAnswer: Alcoholic fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose.
It produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for cellular respiration.

rubric.why: The definition identifies photosynthesis as the process that uses light energy to make food from carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.description: Photosynthesis uses light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition, including the raw materials and use of light energy.

rubric.why: The equation must show the balanced quantities of reactants and products.
rubric.description: Writes the balanced equation for photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation with six molecules each of carbon dioxide and water forming glucose and six molecules of oxygen.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (in the presence of light and chlorophyll)

items.followUp: Why is the electron transport pathway in cellular respiration called a respiratory chain?

rubric.why: Electrons are excited at two photosystems during the light reactions.
rubric.description: The electron pathway involves two photosystems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the involvement of both photosystems.

rubric.why: The changes in electron energy during transfer produce a profile resembling the letter Z.
rubric.description: The electron energy changes give the pathway a Z-shaped profile.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the electron energy profile or pathway resembles a Z.

modelAnswer: Electrons are excited at two photosystems during the light reactions.
Their energy changes during transfer form a Z-shaped profile, so the pathway is called the Z-scheme.
